review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped the simp attributes and the uses of the identity and tower API. I did not run Lean. The findings rest on how simp rewrites subterms before the terms that contain them, and on the inconsistency between the identity API and the tower API. I found no credible loops. The simp lemma `globalSectionsBaseChangeEquiv_tmul` has non-instance `letI` algebra structures in its statement. I could not tell whether simp matches them in practice, so I did not report it.

findings.problem: Only the `.hom` rewrite is simp. It turns `(baseChangeIdentityIso k p).hom` into `pullback.fst ...`, and the companion rules `baseChangeIdentityIso_inv_fst` and `baseChangeIdentityIso_inv_snd` are not simp. Simp rewrites subterms first, so in `e.inv ≫ e.hom` the `.hom` becomes `fst` before `Iso.inv_hom_id` can match. The result `e.inv ≫ fst` is then a normal form that no simp rule simplifies, although `baseChangeIdentityIso_inv_fst` states that it is `𝟙 X`. The `inv ≫ snd` composite likewise stays unsimplified although `baseChangeIdentityIso_inv_snd` says it is `p`. The tower API does the opposite: it makes its hom_fst, hom_snd, inv_fst and inv_snd lemmas all simp (and their reassoc forms), so it is consistent. The identity API is incomplete.
findings.proposed_change: Make the identity API consistent with the tower API. Mark `baseChangeIdentityIso_inv_fst` and `baseChangeIdentityIso_inv_snd` as `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]`. This gives the normal forms `e.inv ≫ fst = 𝟙 X` and `e.inv ≫ snd = p`, so the `.hom` rewrite no longer leaves stuck terms. `baseChangeIdentityIso_inv_fst` is proved with `rw [← baseChangeIdentityIso_hom]`, so it stays valid. Alternatively drop the simp attribute on `_hom` and expose only the composite lemmas.
findings.benefit: Terms that mix `baseChangeIdentityIso`, `.inv` and the pullback projections reduce under plain `simp`. Users no longer need to call `baseChangeIdentityIso_inv_fst` or `baseChangeIdentityIso_inv_snd` by hand, and the identity case has the same interface as the tower case.

findings.problem: The identity-case value lemmas are not simp. These are `globalSectionsBaseChangeIdentityEquiv_apply`, `baseChangeIdentityIso_inv_appTop_fst` and `baseChangeIdentityIso_inv_appTop_snd`. Their tower analogues, `globalSectionsBaseChangeTowerEquiv_apply` and `baseChangeTowerIso_inv_appTop_fst_fst`, are simp. As a result, `globalSectionsBaseChangeEquiv_identity` has to be proved with a chain of manual `rw` steps ending in `rfl`. The tower theorem ends in a single `simp`. The `_apply` lemma is also proved by `rfl`, so it is a natural unfolding rule that does not expand into anything larger. It has the same orientation and shape as the simp-tagged tower lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Tag `globalSectionsBaseChangeIdentityEquiv_apply` with `@[simp]`, as the tower version is. Also tag the two `baseChangeIdentityIso_inv_appTop_*` lemmas with `@[simp]`, given that the `.inv ≫ fst` and `.inv ≫ snd` lemmas become simp as in the first finding. Then the `rw [...]` chain in `globalSectionsBaseChangeEquiv_identity` can be shortened to `simp`.
findings.benefit: Identity base change and tower base change get the same simp interface. Proofs that mention the identity equivalence can use `simp` instead of the exact lemma sequence. The orientation moves from the opaque equivalence to the concrete `inv.appTop`, in the same direction as the tower lemma.
